name: Growing
label: Kranky
lede: A bassist and a left-handed guitarist from Olympia who built cathedral-sized drones out of volume pedals, released tapes meant to be played two at a time, moved to Brooklyn, found a beat, and came back with twenty-minute sides.

eras.title: Olympia, and a lot of volume pedals
eras.text: Growing started in Olympia, Washington, with a bass, a guitar and drums, and a taste for the Velvet Underground, Spacemen 3 and Acid Mothers Temple. Two long, slow, enormous records for Kranky put it on the label of Stars of the Lid and Labradford, and then Kevin Doria and Joe Denardo took the sound to Brooklyn as a duo.

q: basically, our whole band is volume pedals.
years.h: Kevin Doria, Joe Denardo and Zack Carlson start Growing in Olympia
years.p: Doria on bass, Denardo on guitar, Carlson on drums. The songs are slow instrumental drones built from delay and looper pedals, feedback, EBow and phrase samplers run through parallel amps.
years.xp: Denardo is left-handed and Doria right-handed, so on stage they mirror each other. Both run their effects chains into several amps at once for a stereo spread. AllMusic names the Velvet Underground, Spacemen 3 and Acid Mothers Temple as the starting points.

years.h: Growing's Above/Below Sea Level: two tapes meant to play at once
years.p: After a run of self-released tapes, Growing had two cassettes reissued as one release by Michigan's Animal Disguise, plus Above/Below Sea Level, a double cassette built to be played simultaneously.
years.xp: AllMusic compares the idea to [[The Flaming Lips|1f43d76f-8edf-44f6-aaf1-b65f05ad9402]]' Zaireeka, the four-CD album meant for four players at once. AllMusic also lists the Dry Drunk on Woman 7-inch among the early releases.

years.h: The Sky's Run into the Sea · Kranky KRANK060
years.p: Growing recorded its Kranky debut at Headquarters in Olympia from November 2002 to February 2003. Two of its pieces run past 17 minutes.
years.xp: The Discogs credits list Eryn Ross, Joe Denardo and Kevin Doria, with Stefan Simikich co-recording and Kanako Wynkoop on vocal assistance. The track list is printed alphabetically on the sleeve, and the gatefold has Growing embossed on the front.

years.h: Growing moves to Brooklyn as a duo
years.p: After The Sky's Run into the Sea, Joe Denardo and Kevin Doria moved to Brooklyn and the drummer left. AllMusic says they filled the gap with more effects and loops.

years.h: The Soul of the Rainbow and the Harmony of Light · Kranky
years.p: Growing's second Kranky album (KRANK073) was recorded and mixed at home and at Magnetic Park in 2003 and 2004, with Kevin Doria on guitar and bass beside Joe Denardo.
years.xp: Animal Disguise issued a vinyl edition. Early versions circulated as the Early Stages CD-R.

eras.title: Brooklyn, and a pulse
eras.text: In Brooklyn Growing left Kranky for Megablade, Troubleman and The Social Registry. The ten-minute drones got shorter and started to push forward, and in 2008 the duo went to Europe with Boris.

years.p: The first of three Growing albums for Megablade. Conspiracy Records put out Live on CD and double LP the same year.
Kevin Doria's side project Total Life released its first album on Animal Disguise in an edition of 150; a 500-copy vinyl followed in 2007 and Ken Bradshaw in March 2008.
Growing's drones start to shorten on its second Megablade album.
Released jointly with Troubleman Unlimited. Late in 2007 Growing started with The Social Registry on The Social Club Nº 8 7-inch.

years.h: Growing tours Europe and the UK with Boris
years.p: Kevin Doria and Joe Denardo spent April 2008 on the road across Europe and the UK with the Japanese heavy band [[Boris|57652bf8-cfe8-42e7-b9a7-5572a7080d8d]].
After the mini-album Lateral, Growing's full album for The Social Registry swaps ten-minute pieces for tracks of three to seven minutes.

eras.title: A third member and a Vice deal
eras.text: Sadie Laska of the Brooklyn noise band IUD joined with samplers and a microphone, and Growing signed to Vice Records. The drone band now had rhythm, a voice and a single.

years.h: Sadie Laska joins Growing on samplers and microphone
years.p: Sadie Laska of IUD made Growing a trio again. The new line-up recorded PUMPS! with Barry London at O'Cropolis in Brooklyn in 2009.

yt: Growing, Electric Independence teaser (Vice Records TV)
years.h: PUMPS! on Vice Records, led by Camera '84
years.p: Growing's first album with Sadie Laska is rhythm-driven and short-form. The Village Voice covered the single Camera '84, the record and the new member in March.

years.h: Growing plays ATP, picked by Godspeed You! Black Emperor
years.p: [[Godspeed You! Black Emperor|3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4]] chose Growing for the All Tomorrow's Parties weekend it curated in December 2010.

eras.title: Back to two, and twenty-minute sides
eras.text: After a long hiatus Kevin Doria and Joe Denardo, the whole band again, came back with small-run records on Important and Silver Current, and pieces as long as anything they made in Olympia.

years.p: Growing's first album since PUMPS! is two sides of about 20 minutes each, pressed in a numbered edition of 250 with a screen-printed jacket.

years.h: Diptych · Silver Current, twenty years after Olympia
years.p: Kevin Doria and Joe Denardo's limited LP for Silver Current, two decades after Growing started.
Growing's second Silver Current release, a year after Diptych.
